VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Meta.Description: 3D to 2D edge projection layer. Builds the real Env3d solid model off screen, projects it orthographically through three-edge-projection, and paints the resulting linework UNDERNEATH the existing Env2d drawing. Read by the ProjectedEdges bootstrap only - deliberately NOT registered with AppCore__ConfigLoader, so this module owns its own configuration and stays removable as one folder plus two include lines.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Rend.Description: The projection keeps itself up to date. Every change to a lantern schedules a fresh render; a provisional picture of each view appears within a fraction of a second and the exact linework replaces it as it arrives. Nobody presses anything. This became reasonable only once the rewritten backend brought a full three-view render down from around thirty seconds to under two, and it rests on the debounce below: dragging a dimension emits a render per frame, so the work starts only when the shape has been still for RealtimeDebounceMs, and a change arriving mid-render abandons it rather than finishing a projection of a shape that no longer exists. Set Realtime false to return to the original behaviour, where the toolbar button is the only thing that starts a projection - which is the switch to reach for if a machine turns out not to keep up. A render always covers every view listed in Meta.Views, not merely the ones on screen, so switching between the Lantern Editor and the Drawing Editor never finds a blank drawing.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Mode.Description: Which parts of the Env3d solid model are staged for projection. Every flag drives the SAME mesh builder the live 3D viewport uses, so anything switched on here is guaranteed to be the geometry on screen in 3D.
VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Mode.GlazingOccludesNote: Whether staged glazing HIDES what is behind it. Every other staged mesh is both an edge source and an occluder, and glass being double sided is never backface culled, so with this true the glass behaves as a solid wall: correct hidden line removal, and it deletes the ridge and hip beams, the internal joinery and every far side bar from the drawing. At 25 degrees the near slope of glass runs 214mm in front of the ridge beam at its own mid height, so there is nothing marginal about it. False keeps the glass drawing its own pane edges while excluding its triangles from the clip pass, which is what a drawing office does by putting glass on a layer the hidden line calculation ignores. This is the ONE case where the edge set and the occluder set deliberately differ; StageSampler reports both counts so the divergence is visible rather than assumed.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Proj.Description: What counts as a line, and how finely it is drawn. AngleThresholdDegrees is the dihedral angle above which a shared triangle edge counts as a hard edge; higher values keep less linework and cost less time. IncludeIntersectionEdges adds the lines where two solids cut through one another, which is what draws a finial spike against the ridge behind it - it is now computed once per lantern rather than once per view. Measured phase split on a 39k triangle lantern BEFORE the rewrite: 86 percent clipping, 13 percent intersection, 1 percent extraction. EdgeLiftWorldUnits nudges every edge a hair towards the viewer so that a line lying exactly in its own surface is not judged to be hidden by it; it is in stage units (metres) and 1e-6 is one thousandth of a millimetre. IterationTimeMs applies to the legacy backend only.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Cach.Description: Lantern blocks that do NOT change the 3D model and must therefore be excluded from the projection cache key. Lantern__DrawingLayout__Config is the important one: it holds paper size, orientation, scale, gutter shares and the sheet camera, all recorded onto the lantern, so without this list adjusting the sheet layout would discard a render the user had just waited half a minute for. A DENYLIST rather than an allowlist on purpose - a block added later and forgotten here costs a needless re-render, where a forgotten allowlist entry would leave the wrong lantern on screen.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Pers.Description: Storing rendered linework in the project file so it survives between sessions. The block is written onto the lantern it belongs to, carries a fingerprint of the shape that produced it, and is ignored on load if that shape has since changed - see the CacheKey denylist above, which MUST list this block so that writing it does not itself change the fingerprint. Size is the thing to watch: coordinates are stored as plain readable numbers on purpose, so a busy lantern adds a few hundred kilobytes, and a project holds several lanterns. Autosave puts the whole project through localStorage, which has a quota measured in a handful of megabytes across ALL projects, so a ceiling is enforced: a view with more segments than MaxSegmentsPerView, or a block that would exceed MaxKilobytes, is not stored and says so in the console. The linework is still on screen, it simply will not survive the session. Set Enabled false to never store any.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Perf.Description: Who does the work and how it is scheduled. Backend picks the engine: 'cpu' is this module's own kernel spread across web workers and is the default and the reference output; 'webgpu' hands the occlusion pass to the graphics card through the vendored compute implementation and falls back to cpu automatically where WebGPU is missing; 'legacy' is the unmodified vendored generator, kept so the DiffHarness always has something known-good to compare against. MaxWorkers is a ceiling, not a target - the pool takes one fewer than the machine's core count and never more than this. ClipBvhMaxLeafSize is small on purpose: a node test is six comparisons where a triangle test is a plane trim and an overlap solve, so paying for more node tests to avoid triangle tests is the right trade here. YieldEveryMs governs only the main-thread fallback path, where there are no workers to run behind; BvhMaxLeafSize and CacheBoundsTrees apply to the three-mesh-bvh trees that ModelStage primes, which the intersection pass and the legacy backend still use.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Prev.Description: The provisional picture shown while a view is being projected. It is the SAME occluders seen from the SAME direction, rendered by the graphics card in a few milliseconds, placed at exactly the millimetres the vector linework will occupy - so it is truthful about the shape while being obviously not the finished drawing. Deliberately faint: it is a placeholder, and anyone glancing at the screen should be able to tell at once that the real linework has not arrived yet. It is removed the moment a view's exact segments land, and again in a finally block when a render ends for any reason, so it cannot travel into a sheet bake or a PDF. Set Enabled false to wait on a blank drawing instead.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Tool.Description: The Drawing Editor toolbar control. Injected next to Download PDF by this module, never by the Drawing Editor, so the toolbar builder carries no knowledge of this feature. The button walks three states: nothing rendered yet, rendered and shown, rendered and hidden. Showing and hiding a rendered result repaints the live viewports directly rather than re-rendering the sheet, which matters because a sheet render re-captures the 3D snapshot.
VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Tool.TitleRender: Project the 3D model into every orthographic view. Takes several seconds per view.
VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Tool.TitleHide: Hide the projected linework, keeping it ready to show again
VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Tool.TitleShow: Show the projected linework already rendered for this lantern
VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Tool.TitleStale: The lantern has changed since this was rendered. Render again to bring it up to date.

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Prog.Description: REDUNDANT AS OF 07-Aug-2026, KEPT DELIBERATELY. The progress overlay belonged to a projection that took half a minute and had to announce itself. Rendering is now realtime: a provisional picture appears almost at once and the exact linework follows within a second or two, so a full-screen blocking overlay costs more attention than the wait it describes. ShowOverlay is therefore false and the module is dormant - not deleted, because the realtime model has not yet been proven on every machine in the office. If the projection turns out to be slow on other hardware, set Realtime false in the Render block and ShowOverlay true here, and the original press-the-button-and-watch-the-spinner behaviour returns intact. The module and its stylesheet are still loaded and still work; nothing needs rewriting to bring them back.
VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Prog.ErrorText: Projection failed - see the console for details

VghLantern__ProjectedEdges__Config__Appe.Description: Mid grey drafting linework, rgb(60, 60, 60). Stroke width is in true drawing millimetres, matching the Env2d convention, so it scales like real linework rather than staying a fixed screen thickness.
